step_1_decode_the_scenario_id.evidence: data/champions.json Syndra P 'Transcendent': 'Syndra collects Splinters of Wrath ... stacking up to 120 times' and 'At 120 Splinters of Wrath, Syndra achieves Transcendence, increasing her ability power by 15%.' Corroborated by data/champion-audit/batch-e9-1.json Syndra: 'E3 implemented the Transcendent splinter system (splinters option: 120 -> 1.15x AP buff, 40+ Q charges via Q2 slot, 60+ W true damage)' and data/champion-audit/batch-6.json Syndra: 'splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge'.
step_1_decode_the_scenario_id.conclusion: 120 = max splinters, so EVERY Transcendent threshold is active in this scenario: 40 (Q charges), 60 (W true damage), 80 (E scatter angle/slow), 100 (R execute, documented not modeled), 120 (+15% AP).

step_3_the_40_splinter_second_dark_spher.conclusion: At splinters = 120 (>= 40) Syndra enters the fight with two stocked Dark Spheres, and the engine models the second one as a distinct cast slot 'Q2'. A rotation cast timeline at 120 splinters must therefore contain TWO Dark Sphere casts, not one.

step_4_reconstruct_the_timeline.engine_semantics_quoted: docs/math-foundations.md 1.1: 'Ability recasts are scheduled on one shared timeline (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed and no other cast is in progress, and a cast counts when it starts within the window (_schedule_shared_casts) ... resolved greedily by cast order.' Cast times from data/champions.json: Q castTime 'none', W castTime 'none', E 0.25, R 0.25 — no cooldown lets any of Q/W/E return inside the opening burst (Q 7s recharge, W 12-8s, E 15s), so the opening cast_timeline is exactly the cast order, one entry per slot.

step_4_reconstruct_the_timeline.conclusion: The 120-splinter state mandates the second Dark Sphere cast, which shifts every later cast one slot right. Index 2 is Force of Will.

step_5_independent_cross_check_via_the_c.why: The id also says 'custom_order'. The engine exposes a cast_order option written as a slot list — cached evidence: data/champion-audit/batch-p1-3.json, 'Verified: test_p1_review_3.py TestVladimir — Q 176/W 330/R 385 with cast_order R,Q,W,E'.
step_5_independent_cross_check_via_the_c.argument: Whatever the declared order is, 'Scatter the Weak at index 2' is precisely the DEFAULT Q,W,E,R answer — i.e. the value a timeline produces when the custom order (or the Q2 charge, or both) had no effect. A scenario whose entire purpose is to exercise a non-default cast order cannot legitimately reproduce the default third cast. Every non-default reconstruction I can build from cached data that explains a CHANGE at this index lands on the W slot: (a) Q,W,E,R + Q2 inserted after Q; (b) the repo's own documented custom order R,Q,W,E (R->Q->W). Both give 'Force of Will' at index 2.
step_5_independent_cross_check_via_the_c.domain_sanity_check: Syndra's W 'telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere' and her E knocks Dark Spheres back (stun); both consume spheres, so a correct Syndra rotation opens with the Dark Sphere cast(s) and only then spends them. Opening Q, Q(2nd charge), W is the mechanically correct 120-splinter rotation. (data/champions.json Syndra W and E active prose.)

independent_computation.residual_risk: The one reconstruction that would make BOTH values wrong is a custom order that is R-first AND has Q2 auto-inserted after Q (R, Q, Dark Sphere(Q2), W -> index 2 = 'Dark Sphere'). I found no evidence for an R-first Syndra order: the cached R-first precedent is Vladimir, justified there by the Hemoplague damage-amp debuff being applied at fight start (data/champion-audit/batch-p1-3.json), and Syndra's R carries no fight-opening debuff — its only pre-cast rider, the 100-splinter execute, is documented as not modeled ('the fight target never dies', batch-6.json). Syndra's R also consumes live spheres ('grabs up to 4 nearby live ones'), which argues against an R-first order on domain grounds too.
